title: Long horizon: in November Bob asks for 90 minutes "sometime in Q1". Ask Casey for a few Q1 windows first, then fit Bob's calendar to them; the ninety-day window is past the calendar copy.
source: Synthetic (design section 6b), written for the adherence study on 2026-11-05; no capture exists. Calendar generated by scenarios/synthetic/calendar.ts from Bob's weekly pattern (titles, attendees and places in the captured fixtures' anonymized vocabulary), the scheduling policy is plan 39's (Winnie's config at ca6b6ee). The sync rows claim the real 14-day horizon, so every Q1 time is past the copy.

review.answer: Bob, 2026-11-05: ask the party for Q1 windows.
review.question: In November, "sometime in Q1" for 90 minutes. The expectation is to ask you to narrow it (which month or weeks, days to avoid) before anything goes out. Would you rather she ask Casey for a few Q1 windows first and fit your calendar to them?

events.trigger: Bob cc'd you on a new thread to Casey Lindqvist asking for 90 minutes sometime in Q1; the plan is open and nothing has gone out.

thread.text:
Hi Casey,

+Winnie (agent) to find us 90 minutes sometime in Q1 for our annual planning session. Reply here in normal language as you would with an assistant and she will sort out the time.

Bob

expect.basis: Bob's ruling (scenario review, 2026-11-05; kept 2026-11-07: "it should ask Casey for a more specific window, or when to follow up again to get that window"): ask the party for Q1 windows, or for a date to come back. Casey names a few windows first and Winnie fits Bob's calendar to them. The window runs Jan 1 to Mar 31 2027 and the calendar copy ends late in November, so no time can be checked on his side yet.
expect.notes: EDGE: the loop prompt's "Ask Bob only for a decision that is his: ... a time you cannot settle" points this case at Bob, so a C ask_bob follows the prompt as written and is a miss here: the prompt change to request is to ask the party for windows when the horizon is past the calendar copy. check_calendar over the plan window returns nothing checkable (beyond coverage); a model that proposes anyway proposes times nobody checked.
